newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shun Tak's Ho gives thumbs up on HK property.
newsitem.headline: Shun Tak's Ho gives thumbs up on HK property.

text.p: Hong Kong tycoon Stanley Ho said on Tuesday he was confident residential property prices in the territory would stay robust and move higher in 1997.

"For 1997, I'm afraid the market will go up by another 10 percent," Ho, group executive chairman of Shun Tak Holdings, told reporters at a loan signing ceremony of a major residential property redevelopment project.
"The government has allocated this much land, but there are more and more emigrants returning," he said. "They need to buy flats."
The project, Belcher Gardens on Hong Kong island's Pokfulam Road, is being undertaken by developer Ranex Investments Ltd.
Ranex is 51 percent held by Shun Tak and 29 percent by Sun Hung Kai Properties. New World Development Co Ltd and Liu Chong Hing Investment each hold 10 percent.
Seventeen banks signed a HK$6.3255 billion five-year term loan facility for the consortium, half of which would be paid for the land premium and the balance for construction costs.
The loan is guaranteed up to 48.33 percent by Sun Hung Kai and 31.67 percent by Shun Tak, while New World and Liu Chong Hing are responsible for 10 percent each.
The loan pays a margin of 100 basis points over the Hong Kong Interbank Offered Rate (HIBOR) for year one to four and 130 basis points over HIBOR thereafter until maturity.
With fees, the all-in return is 125 basis points over HIBOR, a Shun Tak spokeswoman said.
Arrangers are HSBC Investment Bank Asia, Hang Seng Finance, Westdeutsche Landesbank, Chase Manhattan Asia and China Development Finance Co (HK).
The development will have a site area of 324,271 square feet, gross floor area of 2.44 million square feet and would yield 2,250 units in 10 tower blocks.
While Ho would not say how much the Belcher development would fetch when it is ready in 2000, he said the site was now estimated at between HK$7,000 and HK$8,000 per square foot.
Commenting on recent public pressure placed on the government to control property prices, Ho said there was little the government could do apart from making more land available.
"The government has done almost all it can. The important thing is whether more land can be made available," he said.

Shun Tak is also working on redeveloping another residential project in Chatham Gardens in Kowloon but was yet to raise funds, Ho said, adding the company had yet to complete compensation packages for 15 existing tenants at the site.

Ho is also active in neighbouring Macau, where his company Sociedade de Tourismo e Diversoes de Macau operates the Portuguese-run enclave's nine casinos and its subsidiaries run lotteries as well as the greyhound and horse tracks.
